tests.name: New user can sign up and lands on a funded dashboard
tests.summary:
Created an account as Kane Tester using the provided email address and username.
Confirmed that @kanew3r95g was available before completing registration.
Completed account creation successfully.
Reached the welcome page for Kane, where the wallet balance displayed $500.00.

tests.name: Split a $236 bill four ways and get a link per person
tests.summary:
Created the split requested for “Kane dinner w3r7t9” with a total of $236 and participants zoya, kabir, and sofia.
Confirmed the total was divided among 4 people at $59.00 each.
The new split is listed as “1 of 4 paid,” with zoya, kabir, and sofia each owing $59.00 and each having a Copy link button.

tests.name: Shield blocks a look-alike of a saved contact's address
tests.summary:
Opened the Shield address-check page and entered the provided wallet address.
Checked the address.
The result marked the address as “Blocked” and said it looks like Ada’s saved address but is not the same address.

tests.name: Shield blocks a look-alike of a saved contact's address
tests.summary:
Opened the sign-in page, then went to the address-checking page as requested.
Entered the provided wallet address and selected “Check address.”
The result marked the address as “Blocked” and said it looks like Ada’s saved address but is not.

tests.name: A payment over the spend limit waits for password confirmation
tests.summary:
You asked to send $150 to @ada for rent.
Entered the payment message and selected the $150 payment option.
The confirmation screen showed that the amount exceeded the $100 per-payment limit and the $25 limit for new recipients.
Entered the password and confirmed the payment.
The payment was completed, with the page showing “Sent $150.00 to @ada.”

tests.name: Shield flags a fake Phantom airdrop link as dangerous
tests.summary:
You asked to check the link https://phantorn-airdrop.app/claim using the Quick check option.
The link was entered and checked on the site.
The result marked the link as “Dangerous” and explained that the address imitates Phantom without being the real site.

tests.name: Shield flags a fake Phantom airdrop link as dangerous
tests.summary:
Checked the requested link, https://phantorn-airdrop.app/claim, using the Quick check option.
The scan marked the link as Dangerous.
The displayed reasons stated that the address imitates Phantom but is not the real site.

tests.name: Shield refuses to save a look-alike of a saved person
tests.summary:
Entered the name “Ada new” and the provided wallet address on the People page.
Clicked “Save person.”
The page reported that the address was not saved because it looked like Ada’s saved address.
“Ada new” was not added to the list of people.

tests.name: Paying a name that is both a saved person and another user asks who you meant
tests.summary:
Requested a $5 payment to Semi with the note “coffee.”
Entered “pay semi 5 for coffee” and selected the $5.00 payment option.
The page asked which Semi was intended and showed both the saved contact and the Mlyfo user option.
Selected “Your contact Semi,” and the payment was confirmed as sent.

tests.name: A payment gives a receipt with an ID and a public receipt page
tests.summary:
You asked to open the Receipt link in Recent activity.
Opened the receipt page for a $10.00 payment to @kabir.
The receipt ID shown was MLY-QD8H-FHWX, which begins with “MLY-”.

tests.name: A payment gives a receipt with an ID and a public receipt page
tests.summary:
Opened the Receipt link from Recent activity as requested.
The receipt page confirmed a $10.00 payment to @kabir.
The receipt ID was shown as MLY-ZL2H-P9UG, which begins with “MLY-”.

The sign-in action was completed, and the address-check page opened.

You asked to sign in, open the Shield address-checking page, and check the provided wallet address.
The address was entered and checked on the Shield page.
The result marked the address as “Blocked,” identified it as both an Ethereum and Base address, and warned that it resembles Ada (Base)’s saved address but is not the same address.

The requested sign-in action was completed, then the address-check page was opened.
The address 0x7a3f9cE5b801Dd3fA7426C9e0B1f8a5d3e27c4b9 was entered and checked.
The result marked the address as “Blocked,” identified it as looking like Ada (Base)’s saved address but not matching it, and showed both Ethereum and Base labels.

tests.name: The Android page offers the app install and a safe keyboard download
tests.summary:
Opened the requested Mlyfo web manifest page.
The Mlyfo page included the “Mlyfo on your Android phone” heading, a “Download the keyboard” button, and Chrome installation guidance.
The page also displayed its privacy statements and a SHA-256 download fingerprint.
The web manifest confirmed the app name is “Mlyfo” and its display mode is “standalone”.

tests.name: The Android page offers the app install and a safe keyboard download
tests.summary:
Opened the Mlyfo web manifest and confirmed that the app is named “Mlyfo” with a standalone display mode.
Viewed the Mlyfo Android page, which includes a “Download the keyboard” button and Chrome installation guidance.
Confirmed the page’s safety information: internet is the keyboard’s only permission, keystrokes never leave the phone, and a SHA-256 download fingerprint is provided.
The requested information was successfully reached and verified.
